text: Yeah, rear delts are weird because they're part of the shoulder cap, so there are side delts and front delts as well. I just figured the shoulders were what we were talking about. If you put together all the sets of shoulders, it'll equate to more than 10 sets and an accumulation over a period of time during the week. I think the rear delts also get worked when you do back, so that sounds about right. I wouldn't categorize the rear delt as an individual muscle, so it should always be adaptable. People and coaches should always be able to add more rear delts, I guess, if they wanted, but that's the way I look at it.
